messages:
maria: launching a quick compare across EU-west (SXM) and US-east (PCIe) for mpt-7b fp16 on 2xA100 per node. goal: find where NVLink helps for long-context workloads and spot NUMA/pinning effects.

bench-bot: job started 2026-03-19T09:12 (1799990001) \u2014 config: seqs=[256,512,1024,2048], bs=[1,4,8], runtime=120s per run, kernel=auto, numa=default

aj: first pass (eu-west sxm): seq=1024 bs=8 p50=40ms p95=80ms steady_tps=2.3k. us-east p50=49ms p95=140ms steady_tps=1.7k. notable p95 inflation on PCIe.

sam: nice. were both nodes using the same driver/kernel? any PCIe switch topology differences?

maria: drivers matched, but motherboard vendor differs (us-east uses a board with a PCIe switch between GPUs). initial runs had no explicit cpu/mem pinning. command used:
```
./bench_tool --model mpt-7b --dtype fp16 --gpus 2 --seq 1024 --bs 8 --duration 120 --kernel auto --collect nvlink
```

aj: nvlink traces show heavy inter-gpu memcpy when kv-cache hit ratio >60%. on SXM that stays on the high-bandwidth link, on PCIe it falls back to serializing batches over PCIe root complex -> longer tails.

maria: we saw odd inversion at bs=1 seq=256: PCIe p50 ~9ms vs SXM p50 ~12ms. dug in: CPU thread placement was scattering across sockets and caused extra latency for intra-process DMA on SXM node.

devops-eng: that screams NUMA. were you binding threads? what about iommu/ats settings?

maria: reran with explicit pinning:
```
numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1 ./bench_tool --... --pin numa
```
After pinning: PCIe p50 improved ~10-12%, p95 down ~15%. SXM stayed mostly same (already benefiting from nvlink).

aj: also tried forcing kernels on SXM for long seqs: fused-attn-v2 + cudagraphs gave +9% throughput and p95 -12%. forcing helped stabilize steady-state.

sam: how did quantized runs behave? any kernel selection flips?

maria: yeah — int8 run picked a sparse-optimized attention kernel that ended up being slower for seq>=2048 (unexpected). it changed memory access pattern and increased cross-gpu shuffles. added note: quantization can change kernel choice and thereby topology sensitivity.

bench-bot: attached artifacts: /artifacts/1799990001/nvlink_traces.tgz, /artifacts/1799990001/perf_logs.json

aj: quick takeaways we should capture in onboarding docs:
- SXM wins for medium+ sequence lengths once KV cache reuse drives cross-gpu traffic (lower p95, higher steady TPS).
- PCIe can outperform on short seq/low bs when CPU/NUMA affinity is correct and cross-gpu transfers are minimal.
- Kernel selection materially affects both throughput and topology sensitivity (fused kernels + cudagraphs are best on SXM).
- Quantization may cause a kernel switch -> run kernel-sanity checks as part of onboard CI.

maria: action items:
- microbench: sweep seqs to map NVLink saturation point per model and per node type (mpt-7b, llama-2-7b, mixeval).
- add NUMA pinning snippet and checklist to model onboarding (include numactl examples and how to detect wrong affinity).
- add an automated kernel-validation step to onboarding CI that rejects quant builds if they pick a pathological kernel for long contexts.

sam: I'll open the PR for "kernel & topology" section and add the numactl snippet + example diffs.

devops-eng: scheduling a repeat on us-east with PCIe topology tracing enabled (pci sysfs counters + nvlink counters) — targeting Thurs 10:00 UTC. I'll include the PCIe switch topology dump.

aj: one ops suggestion: can Console surface per-route NVLink utilization or cross-gpu bytes/sec? would help runtime routing decisions.

sam: adding to metrics backlog. we can start with a per-model gauge and a p95 alert when cross-gpu bytes/sec exceeds threshold.

maria: saving charts and raw traces to onboarding artifacts and will paste links in the PR. will follow-up after us-east rerun. :thumbsup: :rocket:

aj: also, note for capacity planning: on SXM steady throughput gains reduce required reserved GPUs by ~15-25% for long-context workloads vs PCIe in our runs — tag that in the capacity sizing playbook.

maria: thanks all, closing this thread for now. will post the repeat results and updated checklist once done.
